page: Microsoft Azure D192s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. This high parallel throughput is supported by strong memory bandwidth, reaching 14141.15 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 673.92 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and PassMark memory scores falling into the middle 50% average. Cryptographic and vector operations are accelerated by hardware flags such as AVX-512, AMX, and AES.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between massive parallel compute capacity and single-threaded execution speeds. While multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations achieve top-tier throughput, LLM text generation speeds are limited, with the small 135M model text generation falling into the bottom 25% tier. However, prompt processing speeds for 7B and 70B models remain strong. Given the lack of local storage and high memory-to-core density, this instance is suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, and parallelized CPU-bound workloads that leverage external premium storage.
